title: Compatible affine charts for the relative affinization of a qcqs morphism
statement: Let $h:Z\to S$ be a quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Put $\mathcal A=h_*\mathcal O_Z$, with $(h_*\mathcal O_Z)(V)=\Gamma(h^{-1}(V),\mathcal O_Z)$ and the $\mathcal O_S$-algebra structure induced by $h$ [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf]. Then $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. There exist an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism] $\pi:Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)\to S$ and an algebra isomorphism $\alpha:\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_*\mathcal O_Y$ with the relative-spectrum chart identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec]. For each affine open $U\subseteq S$ put $Z_U=h^{-1}(U)$ and $Y_U=\pi^{-1}(U)$, and let $q_U:Y_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)$ be the isomorphism induced by $\alpha_U$. There are morphisms $e_U:Z_U\to Y_U$ over $U$ such that $q_U\circ e_U$ is the canonical morphism $j_U:Z_U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(Z_U,\mathcal O_{Z_U})$, namely the unique morphism corresponding to the identity on $\Gamma(Z_U,\mathcal O_{Z_U})$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], using $\mathcal A(U)=\Gamma(Z_U,\mathcal O_{Z_U})$. Writing $\iota_U:Y_U\hookrightarrow Y$ for the open inclusion, the maps $\iota_U\circ e_U:Z_U\to Y$ agree on $Z_U\cap Z_V$ for every pair of affine opens $U,V\subseteq S$. No affineness of $Z_U$ or $U\cap V$, nor quasi-compactness or separation of $S$, is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01LY, lemma-canonical-morphism, canonical morphism and its restrictions to affine opens

proof.text: The structure sheaf $\mathcal O_Z$ is quasi-coherent: on each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Z$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] with $n=1$, and use the affine-local definition [pqf-def-coherent]. Since $h$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] gives quasi-coherence of $\mathcal A=h_*\mathcal O_Z$. Sectionwise multiplication and $h^\sharp$ give its stated commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf].

source.place: Schemes, Tag 01LC (lemma-push-forward-quasi-coherent); Constructions, Tag 01LY (lemma-canonical-morphism), first assertion

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2) to this quasi-coherent algebra. Obtain an affine $\pi:Y\to S$ and an algebra isomorphism $\alpha:\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_*\mathcal O_Y$. Its charts $q_U:Y_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)$ have section maps $\alpha_U$, exactly as required.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-algebra-local-maps] with $f=h$, $g=\pi$ and the algebra-sheaf map $\beta=\alpha^{-1}:\pi_*\mathcal O_Y\to h_*\mathcal O_Z$. It supplies $k_U:Z_U\to Y$ with $\pi k_U=h|_{Z_U}$, agreeing on every overlap. The section map on $Y_U$ is $\beta_U=\alpha_U^{-1}$. The displayed equality over $S$ implies $k_U(Z_U)\subseteq\pi^{-1}(U)=Y_U$; [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] therefore gives a unique $e_U:Z_U\to Y_U$ with $\iota_U e_U=k_U$. It is over $U$ by the same equality and uniqueness of factorization through the open $U\subseteq S$.

source.place: Constructions, Tag 01LY (lemma-canonical-morphism), identity-algebra-map construction; Section 01LL (relative spectrum functor); Schemes, Tag 01HI (lemma-restrict-map-to-opens)

proof.text: The ring map corresponding to $q_U e_U$ is $\mathcal A(U)\xrightarrow{\alpha_U}\Gamma(Y_U,\mathcal O_{Y_U})\xrightarrow{\alpha_U^{-1}}\Gamma(Z_U,\mathcal O_{Z_U})=\mathcal A(U)$, hence is the identity. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], $q_U e_U=j_U$. Finally $\iota_U e_U=k_U$ and $\iota_V e_V=k_V$, so their restrictions to $Z_U\cap Z_V$ agree by step 3. Neither this identity calculation nor the cited local-maps theorem requires $Z_U$ or $U\cap V$ to be affine, or any quasi-compactness or separation of $S$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01LY, lemma-canonical-morphism; algebra-map form of the relative spectrum universal property in section-spec, with the local maps supplied by the existing general affine-algebra local-maps lemma

Step 4: (q_U e_U)^#=alpha_U^{-1} o alpha_U=id, and morphism-into-affine-scheme with arbitrary source gives q_U e_U=j_U.
